mcqs.q: A dental impression is best defined as:
opts: A negative imprint of the teeth and soft tissues from which a positive cast is formed
The positive stone model of the dental arch
A radiograph of the teeth and bone
A wax record of the patient's bite
mcqs.explain: The impression is the NEGATIVE imprint; the cast/model poured from it is the positive reproduction.

mcqs.q: Alginate is classified as:
mcqs.explain: Alginate = irreversible hydrocolloid (elastic); agar = reversible hydrocolloid; ZOE/plaster/compound = non-elastic.

mcqs.q: Which is a NON-elastic impression material?
mcqs.explain: Non-elastic: zinc-oxide eugenol, impression compound, plaster. Alginate/agar are hydrocolloids; polyether is an elastomer.

mcqs.q: During setting, alginate (sodium/potassium alginate) reacts with calcium sulfate to form:
mcqs.explain: Alginate + calcium sulfate → insoluble calcium alginate gel.

mcqs.q: The ingredient added chiefly for strength and body in alginate is:
mcqs.explain: Diatomaceous earth provides strength/body; trisodium phosphate is the retarder.

mcqs.q: The role of trisodium phosphate in alginate is to:
opts: Act as a retarder, delaying gelation until it is consumed
mcqs.explain: The retarder reacts preferentially with calcium sulfate; when consumed, gel formation begins.

mcqs.q: Alginate impressions must be poured immediately because they undergo:
mcqs.explain: Water uptake (imbibition) and loss (syneresis) distort the impression, so pour immediately and keep at 100% humidity.

mcqs.q: The clinician can control alginate's setting time by adjusting the:
mcqs.explain: Higher water temperature speeds the set; lower slows it.

mcqs.q: Which tray feature does NOT provide mechanical retention of alginate?
mcqs.explain: Retention comes from rim locks, perforations, adhesive, or tray extension — not a smooth surface.

mcqs.q: An alginate impression should be removed from the mouth:
opts: Only after the stone has set
mcqs.explain: Remove with a quick snap 2–3 minutes after gelation to avoid tearing/distortion.

mcqs.q: A recommended method to disinfect an alginate impression is:
opts: Spray with glutaraldehyde and seal in a bag ~10 minutes
Leave it to dry in open air overnight
mcqs.explain: Spray glutaraldehyde, seal ~10 min, keep moist, then pour.

mcqs.q: For pouring a diagnostic cast, the recommended material and technique is:
opts: Vacuum-mixed ADA type-4 stone added in small amounts at one location with a vibrator
Fast-set plaster poured all at once
Impression compound melted into the tray
mcqs.explain: Add small increments of vacuum-mixed type-4 stone at one point, using a vibrator to minimize bubbles.

mcqs.q: Using a tray that is TOO SMALL for the arch typically causes:
opts: Soft-tissue displacement, distortion and tearing on removal
The material to stay unconfined over the palate
mcqs.explain: Too small → tissue displacement and distortion; solution is a correctly sized/modified tray.

mcqs.q: An air bubble trapped on an occlusal surface of the impression produces, on the cast, a:
mcqs.explain: A void in the impression casts as a positive nodule; check and carefully remove it.

mcqs.q: A diagnostic cast is:
opts: An accurate replication of the arch showing teeth and surrounding-tissue relationships
A negative imprint of the arch
mcqs.explain: The diagnostic cast is the positive replica used for analysis and planning.

mcqs.q: Which is a use of an articulated diagnostic cast in fixed prosthodontics?
opts: Rehearsing tooth preparations and performing a diagnostic wax-up
Replacing the need for any clinical exam
mcqs.explain: Uses: occlusal analysis, abutment evaluation, prep rehearsal, diagnostic wax-up (→ putty index), and custom-tray fabrication.

mcqs.q: Chemically, alginates are:
opts: Sodium or potassium salts of alginic acid, and therefore water-soluble
Calcium salts of alginic acid, and therefore insoluble
mcqs.explain: They react with calcium sulfate to produce insoluble calcium alginate in a very quick reaction.

mcqs.q: The product of the alginate setting reaction is:
mcqs.explain: Diatomaceous earth is added chiefly for strength and body.

mcqs.q: Why must teeth be cleaned of plaque and debris before an alginate impression?
opts: A clean field gives an accurate imprint
It speeds up the setting reaction
It prevents the alginate bonding chemically to enamel
mcqs.explain: Excess saliva is absorbed with gauze after rinsing.

mcqs.q: Before and after pouring with gypsum products, an alginate impression should be stored at:
mcqs.explain: This limits both syneresis and imbibition.

mcqs.q: The impression should be separated from the cast after:
mcqs.explain: For alginate, the best results are obtained if the cast is removed at one hour.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a way of retaining alginate in the tray?
opts: Chemical bonding of alginate to the tray material
A rim-lock beading round the edges
Perforations — holes or slits in the tray
Applying a liquid or spray adhesive
mcqs.explain: Alginate does not bond chemically, which is exactly why mechanical features or adhesive are needed.

mcqs.q: Applying a small amount of alginate to the occlusal crevices with the index finger before seating:
opts: Reduces air voids and improves accuracy
Speeds up gelation at the occlusal surface
Prevents the tray from seating too deeply
Improves the bond of alginate to the tray
mcqs.explain: Loading the tray by pressing and swiping forces material through the perforations, locking it mechanically.

mcqs.q: During seating, if the patient stretches wide open:
opts: Material is often squeezed out of the mucobuccal fold or from under the upper lip
mcqs.explain: The patient should be reminded to relax the cheek muscles.

mcqs.q: An alginate impression should be removed:
mcqs.explain: A rapid single movement allows the elastic material to recover; a slow pull causes permanent deformation.

mcqs.q: When pouring the cast, adding the stone consistently at the same spot:
opts: Speeds the setting of the stone
Prevents the cast adhering to the impression
mcqs.explain: A vacuum-mixed ADA type 4 stone is recommended, added at one location such as the posterior of a molar, with a vibrator to reduce bubbles.

mcqs.q: Using a tray that is TOO LARGE may mean that:
opts: The material is not confined to the soft tissues, and the tray is hard to seat posteriorly
The impression cannot be removed without tearing
The tray separates from the impression on removal
mcqs.explain: The other three are the problems of a tray that is too small. The tray should stand a few millimetres away from the tissues.

mcqs.q: Distortion caused by part of the impression being unsupported by the tray is solved by:
opts: Extending the tray and modifying its perimeter with modeling compound
mcqs.explain: Tray movement during setting produces the same distortion.

mcqs.q: If the teeth are excessively dried before an alginate impression:
opts: The impression tears more easily on removal
mcqs.explain: The solution is simply not to over-dry the teeth.

mcqs.q: A patient with a high gag reflex is best managed by:
opts: Correct tray size, minimal material, posterior seated first, upright, nasal breathing
Using the largest tray available so it seats quickly
Seating the anterior region first and tilting the head back
Using warmer mixing water to speed up the set
mcqs.explain: Reducing the volume of material and the time it sits posteriorly is the key.

mcqs.q: Which is a stated use of a diagnostic cast?
opts: Rehearsing tooth preparations on the cast
mcqs.explain: Diagnostic casts also allow static and dynamic occlusion to be examined from all directions, abutment alignment and angulation to be evaluated, a diagnostic wax-up to preview the outcome, a putty index for provisionals, and a custom tray to be made.

saqs.q: Define a dental impression and classify impression materials (with an example of each main group).
saqs.a: An IMPRESSION is a negative imprint of the hard and soft tissues, from which a positive cast is made. NON-ELASTIC (rigid) — ZOE, impression compound, plaster. ELASTIC elastomers — polysulfide, silicone, polyether. ELASTIC hydrocolloids — reversible (agar), irreversible (alginate).

ans.text: A negative imprint of the hard and soft tissues, from which a positive cast is made.

saqs.q: Describe the setting reaction of alginate and explain why the impression must be poured immediately.
saqs.a: Sodium/potassium alginate reacts with calcium sulfate to form insoluble CALCIUM ALGINATE (gel); trisodium phosphate is a retarder until consumed, then gelation begins. Pour immediately because IMBIBITION (water uptake) and SYNERESIS (water loss) distort the impression; store at 100% humidity.

ans.text: Sodium/potassium alginate reacts with calcium sulfate to form insoluble calcium alginate (gel). Trisodium phosphate acts as a retarder until consumed, after which gelation begins.

saqs.q: List five guidelines for making a good alginate impression.
saqs.a: Rigid, sturdy perforated or rim-lock trays · clean teeth (remove plaque, rinse, absorb saliva) · a uniform homogeneous mix · fill the tray sufficiently with no voids · a good tray–material bond · pour as soon as possible (100% humidity, separate after 60 min).

list: Ensure the teeth are clean — remove plaque, rinse, absorb saliva
Pour as soon as possible — store at 100% humidity, separate after 60 min

saqs.q: Give three problems associated with alginate impressions and a solution for each.
saqs.a: Tray too small → tissue displacement/distortion → use a suitable size or modify the tray. Unsupported material or tray movement → distortion → extend the tray and modify its perimeter with modeling compound. Air void → nodule on the cast → check and carefully remove nodules. (Also: sets too fast → adjust water temperature; over-dried teeth adhere → do not over-dry.)

head: Problem
Result
Solution
rows: use a suitable size, or modify the tray
extend the tray and modify its perimeter with modeling compound
check the cast and carefully remove nodules

saqs.q: Define a diagnostic cast and list four of its uses in fixed prosthodontics.
saqs.a: A DIAGNOSTIC CAST is an accurate replication of the arch showing the relationships of teeth and surrounding tissues. Uses: analyse static and dynamic occlusion on an articulator · evaluate abutment alignment and angulation · rehearse tooth preparations · perform a diagnostic wax-up and make a putty index · fabricate a custom tray.

ans.text: An accurate replication of the arch, showing the relationships of the teeth and surrounding tissues.

list: Analyse static and dynamic occlusion on an articulator
Perform a diagnostic wax-up, and make a putty index

saqs.q: Describe the guidelines for making a good alginate impression.
saqs.a: 1 Rigid, sturdy trays with perforations or a rim-lock — alginate does not bond chemically, so mechanical retention is essential. 2 Clean teeth — remove plaque and debris, rinse, absorb saliva. 3 A uniform homogeneous mix free of streaks. 4 Sufficiently fill the tray. 5 No voids — material forced through the perforations both retains itself and avoids surface bubbles.

head: Guideline
Why
rows: RIGID, STURDY TRAYS with perforations or rim-lock
rigid trays resist flexing; perforations or rim-lock give the mechanical retention alginate needs, since it does not bond chemically to the tray
remove plaque and debris, rinse, absorb excess saliva with gauze — a clean field gives an accurate imprint
free of streaks, so it sets evenly and records fine detail
material forced through the perforations both retains itself and avoids surface bubbles

saqs.q: Describe the procedure for pouring an alginate impression, including disinfection.
saqs.a: Rinse and DISINFECT — glutaraldehyde spray, self-sealing bag, ~10 minutes. Dry slightly and pour IMMEDIATELY, keeping it wet (wet gauze) until pouring. Use VACUUM-MIXED ADA TYPE 4 STONE. Add a small amount at ONE location (e.g. posterior of a molar) — always the same spot minimises bubbles. Use a VIBRATOR, fill with the remaining stone and set aside. Store at 100% humidity; for alginate remove the cast at ONE HOUR.

steps: Rinse and DISINFECT — spray with a suitable glutaraldehyde and place in a self-sealing plastic bag for about 10 minutes
Dry slightly with a gentle air stream and pour IMMEDIATELY, keeping the impression in a wet environment (wet gauze) until pouring
Add a small amount at ONE location — e.g. the posterior of a molar; adding consistently at the same spot minimises bubbles
Use a VIBRATOR to reduce bubbles, fill with the remaining stone and set aside
Store at 100% humidity; for alginate the best results come from removing the cast at ONE HOUR
